executive_summary: Business survived the full 2016-2025 window including the 2021-22 crisis. Net margin £166,705 (19.4% of total revenue -- above 2-5% benchmark). Hedging cost £238,162 vs going naked (85% mandate price). 1541 bill shock events (406 in crisis years); 16/31 retention offers accepted.

insights.headline: Hedging cost £238,162 vs going naked (85% mandate price)
insights.narrative: Whole-run commodity basis: actual net £151,057 vs naked £389,218. The 85% minimum hedge mandate cost £238,162 over the 10-year window. Worst year: 2023 (hedging cost £43,835 vs naked). Hedging reduces variance (survival objective) at the cost of expected P&L.

insights.headline: 1541 bill shock events (406 in crisis years); 16/31 retention offers accepted
insights.narrative: Bill shocks across 2016-2025: 1541 events, 589 extreme (>100%). 2021-22 accounted for 406 shocks as wholesale prices spiked. Retention: 16/31 offers accepted (52%); 26 customers churned without an offer (margin guard blocked). Enterprise value: £165,174 across 60 accounts.

insights.headline: Risk committee: 0 interventions; SURVIVED full 2016-2025 window
insights.narrative: The risk committee (Context Handshake) intervened 0 times over 10 years, with 0 in the 2021-22 crisis. Business survived: No administration event -- Ofgem solvency floor maintained.. The 85% minimum hedge mandate limited worst-case exposure.

insights.headline: Net margin £166,705 (19.4% of total revenue -- above 2-5% benchmark)
insights.narrative: Gross margin £419,913, net £166,705 (19.4% of revenue). Industry benchmark: 2-5% -- this business sits above that range. I&C customers contribute 0% of net margin (£0); residential 100% (£166,705). Cost to serve: £47,909; net after CTS: £118,796.

insights.headline: 10595 bills issued; service quality 0.930/1.0, clarity 0.878/1.0
insights.narrative: 10595 bills issued over 2016-2025 (avg 1060/yr). Service quality: 0.930 (excellent). Bill clarity: 0.878 (good). Cost to serve: £47,909 portfolio total, £798/account/run.

coherence_narrative: The dominant theme is crisis survival. The business survived the full 2016-2025 window including the 2021-22 energy crisis, with the 85% hedge mandate cost £238,162 vs going naked, 406 bill shocks in the 2021-22 crisis, and 16/31 retention offers accepted. net margin £166,705 (19.4% of revenue -- above 2-5% benchmark), with I&C customers contributing 0% of net margin. The hedging mandate limited worst-case downside at the cost of expected P&L in calmer years; the I&C book was the primary profit engine throughout. The book is well-diversified between residential and I&C segments.
recommended_actions: I&C margin share 0%: diversified book -- maintain residential acquisition to keep I&C below 70% dependency
Hedge cost £238,162 over 10 years -- mandate is a survival insurance premium, not an expected-value strategy
406 crisis-year bill shocks: consider tariff smoothing mechanism to spread 2021-22 wholesale spike across 2020-2023 for residential customers
